title: How much evidence is one event? A Bayesian and frequentist reassessment of the LZ 248 keV recoil
question: What Bayes factor and posterior DM probability does one event in a region with modelled background ~2e-4 (whole S1c>500 phd panel 0.0106) support, and how does it depend on the signal prior, the prior probability of DM in this window, and an unknown-background nuisance?
headline_result: B10 = 1 + E_pi[s e^-s]/b = 100-500 against the modelled background (b = 1e-3 to 2e-4, flat s in [0,10]) but 7-37 after a ~14-fold Occam penalty for the tested spectra, consistent with the Sellke-Bayarri-Berger cap of 14.7 from LZ's 2.6 sigma global p; the posterior is set by pi_DM*E vs pi_U*L_U (P(DM)>1/2 needs pi_DM > 10 pi_U L_U) and is 0.09 for pi_DM=0.01, pi_U L_U=0.01
model_or_mechanism: Poisson-in-a-box single-event inference; closed-form Bayes factor; 2- and 3-hypothesis posteriors with unknown-background alternative; mixture Occam factor vs frequentist LEE; SBB p-value calibration
agent_tools: Read x7, Bash x8, Write x4, Edit x8, Skill x1 (dataviz)
